# Issue #41: `slugify` produces double hyphens and trailing hyphens

`slugify("Hello,  World!")` returns `"hello--world-"` but should return `"hello-world"`.
Also `slugify("--a--b--")` should give `"a-b"`.

Please fix `textkit/slug.py`. Do not change the public signature.

The bug is clear: the regex replaces each non-alphanumeric character with a hyphen, but never collapses runs of hyphens or strips leading/trailing ones. Fix:

text = text.lower()

content: Now let me verify the final state of the file:

1| import re
   2| 
   3| def slugify(text: str) -> str:
   4|     """Turn arbitrary text into a URL slug: lowercase, ASCII letters and
   5|     digits, words separated by single hyphens, no leading/trailing hyphens."""
   6|     text = text.lower()
   7|     text = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", text)
   8|     return text.strip("-")

The fix is verified against all cases:

- `slugify("Hello,  World!")` → lowercase → `"hello,  world!"` → `[^a-z0-9]+` collapses the comma+spaces run into a single `-` and `!` into `-` → `"hello-world-"` → `strip("-")` → `"hello-world"` ✓
- `slugify("--a--b--")` → runs of hyphens collapse to single `-` → `"-a-b-"` → `strip("-")` → `"a-b"` ✓
- `slugify("Hello World")` → `"hello-world"` ✓ (existing test still passes)

The public signature `slugify(text: str) -> str` is unchanged; only the regex gained a `+` quantifier and a `strip("-")` was added.

arguments.summary: Fixed slugify in textkit/slug.py by changing the regex from `[^a-z0-9]` to `[^a-z0-9]+` so consecutive non-alphanumeric characters collapse into a single hyphen, and adding `.strip("-")` to remove leading/trailing hyphens. This makes `slugify("Hello,  World!")` return `"hello-world"` and `slugify("--a--b--")` return `"a-b"` while keeping the public signature unchanged.
